reason: Focused process for registering a claimant as owner where entitlement comes from judgment, enactment, sale, mortgage default, or another proceeding.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Registration of claimant as owner
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections identify when documents are filed and forwarded and when the Registrar General orders claimant registration.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how a claimant may be registered as owner of land, an estate, or an interest.

reason: Transmission on death has distinct registration, personal-representative authority, purchaser-protection, and approval topics.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Registration of transmission on death
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections require registration in the personal representative name, prescribed application and documents, interest-only registration, and Registrar General approval.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how registered land or an interest is transmitted on death.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Personal representative instruments and purchaser protection
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections restrict instruments executed by personal representatives unless rights are established and protect good-faith value purchasers.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Describe when a personal representative may execute instruments and how purchasers from a personal representative are protected.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Devolution of Estates Act provisions for transmission
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 53(8) separately applies specified Devolution of Estates Act sections to transmission on death.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the external devolution provisions applied to transmission on death.

reason: The implied-covenants section separates specific implied covenants from their general force, joint liability, and pleading effect.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Implied covenants in transfers and mortgages
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections imply covenants to give effect to instruments, further transfer or mortgage land, and assume mortgage obligations on transfer.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the covenants implied in registered transfers and mortgages.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Force, joint liability, and pleading of implied covenants
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections give implied covenants force as if written, bind multiple parties jointly and severally unless modified, and allow pleading them as expressed.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how implied covenants are enforced, bind parties, and may be pleaded.

reason: Proof of execution divides into signing and proof requirements, who may take affidavits or certificates, and exceptions or electronic-instrument treatment.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Signing and proof of execution for registration
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections set signing or corporate seal requirements and proof by affidavit or certificate in prescribed form.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain the execution and proof documents generally required for registration.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Exceptions, Registrar General direction, and electronic instrument proof
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections exempt listed instruments, allow Registrar General direction where due execution is satisfactory, and apply paper proof rules to electronic-instrument source documents.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify exceptions to execution proof and how electronic instrument source documents are treated.

reason: Focused address-for-service rule for registered or filed instruments and changes of name or address.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Address for service in land titles filings
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections require addresses, allow name or address change notices, and make the last address on file the service address.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: State how addresses for service are supplied and updated for land titles notices.

reason: Focused method-of-service rule for specified Registrar General or registrar notices and other Act notices or documents.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Method of service for land titles notices and documents
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections use Rules of Court personal service methods or directions by the Registrar General.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how required land titles notices and documents are served.

reason: Trust registration rule requiring in-trust registration and Registrar General satisfaction before trust dispositions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Registered land held in trust
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections require registration followed by in trust and block dispositions unless consistent with the trust.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how registered land taken in trust is registered and later disposed of.

reason: Rule limiting trust notices on the title register except as otherwise provided by the Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Treatment of trust notices on the title register

evidenceText: no memorandum, entry or record shall be made upon the title register of any notice of trust
registered as the absolute and beneficial owner

proposedGroups.reason: The text bars title-register trust notices and directs registrar treatment of instruments containing them.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: State how trust notices are treated on the title register unless the Act provides otherwise.

reason: Focused paper-instrument rule about execution without seal or consideration and corporate seal exception.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Seals and consideration for prescribed paper instruments
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections allow prescribed paper instruments without seal or stated consideration, give them sealed-instrument effect, and preserve corporate seal requirements.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain when paper instruments may be executed without seal or stated consideration and when corporate seals are required.

reason: Central protection rule for persons dealing with registered owners against unregistered interests and Personal Property Registry registrations, subject to fraud.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Effect of unregistered instruments, interests, and Personal Property Registry registrations
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections state non-inquiry and no-notice rules for unregistered claims, knowledge not being fraud by itself, and similar treatment for Personal Property Registry registrations.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how unregistered interests and Personal Property Registry registrations affect persons dealing with registered owners.

reason: The target contains only a repeal note.
Focused certificate-of-registered-ownership rule covering who may require it, contents, and evidentiary effect.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Certificate of registered ownership
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections address issuance on request and fee, certificate contents, and evidentiary status.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how certificates of registered ownership are issued and used as evidence.

reason: Single co-ownership rule requiring instruments to state joint tenancy or tenancy in common and giving a default if they do not.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Instrument to state joint tenancy or tenancy in common

evidenceText: joint tenants or as tenants in common
take in accordance with the Property Act

proposedGroups.reason: The text requires stated tenancy for grants, transfers, conveyances, or assignments to two or more persons.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: State what an instrument must say about co-ownership tenancy and the default if it does not.

reason: Single survivorship rule for registering land or interests in the name of surviving joint tenants.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Survivorship in joint tenancy

evidenceText: register the land or interest therein in the name of the survivor

proposedGroups.reason: The text sets the application and document requirement for survivor registration after a joint tenant dies.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how survivorship in joint tenancy is registered.

reason: Focused No Survivorship entry rule limiting dispositions and authorizing court orders for protection of beneficial interests.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Entry of No Survivorship on the title register
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections allow the entry, define No Survivorship, and describe court notice and transfer or protective orders.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain the effect of a No Survivorship entry and the court order process.

reason: Focused rule barring actions to recover registered land from the owner except for listed mortgage, lease, and fraud situations.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Actions for ejectment or recovery of registered land

evidenceText: No action of ejectment or other action for the recovery of registered land shall lie

proposedGroups.reason: The text states the bar on recovery actions and identifies mortgagee, lessor, and fraud exceptions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify when an action to recover registered land may be brought against the owner.

reason: Registrar rectification rule covering consent, specified error or mistake cases, survey dimension errors, and notice to affected persons.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Cases where the registrar may rectify the title register

evidenceText: with the consent of all persons interested
shall first give notice of his intention to rectify

proposedGroups.reason: The text lists when the registrar may rectify and requires notice before rectification in the listed cases.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: State when the registrar may rectify the title register and what notice is required.

reason: Registrar power to cancel entries that no longer affect title and recall or correct documents issued in error.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Registrar powers to cancel entries and recall documents

evidenceText: cancel any entry in the title register
recall a document issued by him

proposedGroups.reason: The text authorizes cancellation of spent entries and recall, correction, or cancellation of erroneous documents.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the registrar powers to cancel title-register entries and recall documents.
